q: How many committees did the Constituent Assembly set up to draft the Constitution of India?
explanation: The Constituent Assembly appointed eight committees in 1946 to draft different parts of the Constitution, the Drafting Committee being the most important of them.

q: The 'Advisory Committee' of the Constituent Assembly was headed by:
explanation: Sachchidananda Sinha, a prominent advocate, chaired the Advisory Committee which dealt with the better future political structure of India; B. N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser to the Assembly.

q: Who was designated the Chief Draftsman of the Constitution of India?
explanation: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar was designated the Chief Draftsman, a role he relinquished in 1950; B. N. Rau prepared the initial draft as Constitutional Adviser before the Drafting Committee took over.

q: The original handwritten Constitution of India was published in how many languages?
explanation: The original Constitution, calligraphed by the calligraphers of the Legislative Department, was published in English and 13 alternative Hindi versions, making fourteen languages in total.

q: The Preamble to the Constitution of India was amended for the first time by which Amendment Act?
explanation: The First Amendment Act of 1951 amended Article 368 and added the words 'Sovereign' and 'Democratic' to the Preamble, which was the first amendment made to it.

q: In the Kesavananda Bharati case, the Supreme Court held that the Preamble:
options: is a part of the Constitution
is not a part of the Constitution
can be amended only by a simple majority of Parliament
is a part of the Constitution only from the date of the 42nd Amendment
explanation: The majority opinion in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution and can be amended under Article 368, though it cannot destroy the basic structure.

q: Article 21C of the Constitution of India provides for:
options: The right to a clean environment
Free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years
Early childhood care and development of children below six years of age
explanation: Article 21C, inserted by the 86th Amendment Act of 2002, provides for early childhood care and development below the age of six; Article 21A deals with education between six and fourteen years.

q: Article 23(2) of the Constitution of India provides that:
options: the bonded labour system is abolished by law
violation of clause (1) shall be a punishable offence
children below fourteen years of age shall not work in factories
the right to work is a fundamental right for all citizens
explanation: Article 23(1) prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour, and clause (2) makes its violation a punishable offence; abolition of bonded labour was achieved through statute.

q: Article 19(2) of the Constitution permits reasonable restrictions in the interest of all EXCEPT:
explanation: The grounds in Article 19(2) are sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality and prevention of incitement to an offence; protection of the environment is not a listed ground.

q: Which Article, inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, was declared void by the Supreme Court in the ADM Jabalpur case?
explanation: Article 32A, which enabled preventive detention for the preservation of national security, was inserted by the 42nd Amendment and struck down by the Supreme Court in ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla (1976).

q: Article 18(2) of the Constitution of India provides that a person holding an office under the State:
options: may accept a military title after five years of service in the army
shall not retain any title after ceasing to hold office
shall not accept any title from a foreign State at all
shall not, without the consent of the President, accept any title from a foreign State
explanation: Article 18(1) abolishes titles, while Article 18(2) bars acceptance of any title from a foreign State without the consent of the President; the prohibition does not extend to military or academic distinctions.

q: Article 30A of the Constitution of India protects:
options: the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
the right of the State to acquire private property for public purposes
the freedom of the press and the freedom of speech
the right to form trade unions and associations
explanation: Article 30A, inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, protects the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

q: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 inserted Article 43A, which deals with:
options: the right to work, education and public assistance
the promotion of cottage industries in rural areas
participation of workers in the management of industries
explanation: Article 43A provides for the participation of workers in the management of industries; Article 42 deals with co-operative societies and Article 43 with cottage industries in rural areas.

q: Article 41 of the Constitution of India directs the State to secure:
options: the right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases
a social order in which social, economic and political justice informs all institutions
explanation: Article 41 directs the State to secure the right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases; the social order clause appears in Article 38.

q: Article 42 of the Constitution of India directs the State to promote:
options: a uniform civil code for the citizens
the participation of workers in the management of industries
the raising of the level of living of workers
explanation: Article 42 asks the State to promote the promotion of co-operative societies, while Article 43A deals with workers' participation in management and Article 44 with a uniform civil code.

q: Article 37 of the Constitution of India provides that the Directive Principles of State Policy:
options: apply only to the Union Government and not to the States
shall not be enforceable by any court but shall be the guiding principles of the State
are enforceable in the High Courts on a discretionary basis
are enforceable by the Supreme Court through writs
explanation: Article 37 makes the Directive Principles non-justiciable but fundamental in the governance of the country, and they apply to the Union as well as to the States.

q: Article 45 of the Constitution, as it originally stood, directed the State to provide free and compulsory education for children up to the age of:
explanation: Original Article 45 promised free and compulsory education for children up to fourteen years; it was substituted by the 86th Amendment Act of 2002 in the light of the RTE Act.

q: The Fundamental Duties added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 are:
options: enforceable in the High Courts only
not enforceable at all, being merely moral obligations
enforceable in courts of a different kind
enforceable in the Supreme Court only
explanation: In Kirpal Singh v. State of Punjab (1962) the Supreme Court held that Fundamental Duties are not enforceable by courts directly but courts may enforce them in a 'different kind' of proceedings.

q: Article 371 of the Constitution, as it stood before 2019, provided special provisions with respect to:
explanation: Article 371 granted special provisions to Jammu and Kashmir; Article 371A covers Sikkim, 371B Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram, and 371C Nagaland.

q: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Amendment Act, 2023 (107th Amendment) provides for:
options: nomination of members of the Scheduled Tribes to the legislatures of certain States
reservation of tribal judges in the High Courts
extension of the 73rd Amendment to the tribal areas of Assam
creation of tribal universities in the Fifth Schedule areas
explanation: The 107th Amendment enables the nomination of Scheduled Tribe members to the legislatures of the listed States, filling the gap left by the delimitation freeze in the Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas.

q: The 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003 added to the Eighth Schedule the languages:
explanation: The 92nd Amendment added Bhojpuri, Maithili, Dogri and Sanskrit to the Eighth Schedule, raising the number of scheduled languages to 22; the others were already scheduled.

q: Article 279A(9A), inserted by the 101st Amendment Act, provides for:
options: the power of the GST Council to levy GST on inter-State supplies
the apportionment of the proceeds of GST between the Union and the States
the power of Parliament to levy GST in the States
compensation to the States for loss of revenue on account of GST
explanation: Sub-article (9A) of Article 279A provides for compensation to any State in case of a reduction in its share of tax revenue on account of the implementation of GST, as recommended by the GST Council.

q: The Inter-State Council is chaired by the:
options: Governor of the State in which the Council meets
explanation: Article 263 provides for the Inter-State Council, which is chaired by the Prime Minister and investigates and advises on questions of common interest to several States.

q: Articles 395 and 396, inserted by the 26th Amendment Act of 1971, abolished:
options: the office of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
the office of the Governor-General of India
the Legislative Councils of the States
the jurisdiction of the Privy Council and privy purses
explanation: The 26th Amendment abolished the Privy Council's jurisdiction for India and the privy purses of the erstwhile princely rulers; Legislative Councils are dealt with by Article 169.

q: The President's Rule in a State can continue for a maximum period of:
explanation: Under Article 356, President's Rule can continue for one year with an extension of one year at a time with the approval of both Houses, but it cannot exceed three years in all.

q: The Lok Sabha was first constituted on:
explanation: The first Lok Sabha was constituted after the first general elections in 1952 and held its inaugural sitting on 17 April 1952; the Rajya Sabha was constituted on 3 April 1952.

q: The Business Advisory Committee of the Lok Sabha, which recommends the sequence and priority of business, is chaired by the:
options: Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Leader of the House in the Lok Sabha
explanation: The Business Advisory Committee is a non-financial committee constituted by the Speaker, who chairs it, along with the Leader of the House, the Leader of the Opposition and other members.

q: A no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers in the Lok Sabha requires the support of at least:
options: one-tenth of the total strength of the House
explanation: Under the Rules of Procedure, a no-confidence motion can be moved only with the support of at least fifty members, and the Council of Ministers is entitled to a fixed reply.

q: Which of the following is NOT a financial committee of the Parliament of India?
explanation: The Committee on Petitions is a non-financial committee that examines petitions relating to matters of public interest; the Estimates Committee, Financial Advisory Council and Committee on Public Undertakings are financial committees.

q: Under Article 100(3), if the House is dissolved before the expiry of its five-year term, the House is deemed to have completed:
explanation: Article 100(3) provides that where a House is dissolved before the expiry of its five-year term, it is deemed to have completed five years, which prevents the incumbent government from seeking a fresh mandate.

q: The salaries of judges of the Supreme Court and of the High Courts are charged on:
options: the Consolidated Fund of the State concerned
explanation: Salaries, allowances and pensions of Supreme Court and High Court judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, though they are not subject to the vote of either House of Parliament.

q: In the Golak Nath case (1967), the Supreme Court held that:
options: Article 32 is not itself a fundamental right
Parliament may abridge Fundamental Rights by a simple majority
the basic structure doctrine applies to every amendment
Fundamental Rights have a transcendental position and cannot be abridged by ordinary legislation
explanation: I.C. Golak Nath v. State of Punjab (1967) held that Fundamental Rights have a transcendental and immutable position, and Parliament cannot abridge them by ordinary legislation.

q: The Maneka Gandhi case (1978) is significant for propounding:
options: the right to legal aid and a wide interpretation of Article 21
the right to privacy as a fundamental right
the doctrine of separation of powers
the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court cannot be curtailed by Parliament
explanation: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) expanded Article 21 to include the right to a speedy trial, a free legal aid and the right to know the reasons for one's detention.

q: In the A.K. Gopalan case (1950), the Supreme Court held that:
options: Fundamental Rights are enforceable only through Article 32
personal liberty under Article 21 is narrow and confined to protection against unlawful arrest
the Constitution confers a broad right to privacy
the basic structure doctrine applies to every amendment
explanation: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras (1950) treated personal liberty under Article 21 as a narrow right confined to protection against unlawful arrest, a view later overruled by Maneka Gandhi.

q: The oath of office of the President of India is administered by:
options: the Chief Justice of India or, in his absence, the senior-most available judge
the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
explanation: Article 60 requires the oath of office to the President to be administered by the Chief Justice of India or, in his absence, the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court available.

q: The retirement age of a judge of a High Court in India is:
explanation: Under Article 217 a High Court judge holds office until he attains the age of sixty-two years, while a Supreme Court judge retires at sixty-five years.

q: A High Court may be established for two or more States by:
options: the Supreme Court by administrative order
explanation: Article 231 enables Parliament by law to establish a High Court for two or more States or for a State and a Union Territory, and to curtail the jurisdiction of an existing High Court.

q: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 provides for reservation of seats for women in:
options: the Lok Sabha and the state legislative assemblies
the Rajya Sabha and the legislative councils
all elected offices including the judiciary
explanation: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provides for one-third of the seats in the Lok Sabha and in state legislative assemblies to be reserved for women, including within seats reserved for SCs and STs.

q: Under the 106th Amendment Act of 2023, the reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha will take effect after the next delimitation exercise undertaken on the basis of:
options: the first census conducted after the commencement of the amendment
explanation: The amendment ties the implementation of women's reservation to the first census held after the law comes into force, so that the seat freeze on population can be applied at that delimitation.

q: In the Kihoto Hollohan case (1992), the Supreme Court held that the decision of the Speaker under the Tenth Schedule:
options: may be overridden by the President
is final and is not subject to any review
binds only the concerned House and the Speaker
is subject to judicial review by the Supreme Court
explanation: Kihoto Hollohan v. Union of India (1992) held that the decision of the Speaker or Chairman on disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is subject to judicial review by the Supreme Court.

q: A candidate for the office of President of India must be a citizen of India and have completed the age of:
explanation: Article 58 prescribes the qualifications of the President, including completion of thirty-five years of age; the same minimum age applies to the Vice-President.

q: The 87th Amendment Act of 2003 read with the 84th Amendment Act of 2001 freezes the allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha and the state assemblies on the basis of the population as per the 1971 census until:
explanation: The freeze on readjustment of seats on the basis of population continues till 2026, and the 106th Amendment of 2023 links the first census after that date to the implementation of women's reservation.

q: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Chairperson of the Lokpal shall be:
options: an existing or retired judge of the Supreme Court or a Chief Justice of a High Court
any person recommended by the Comptroller and Auditor General
explanation: Section 4 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 provides that the Chairperson of the Lokpal shall be an existing or retired judge of the Supreme Court or a Chief Justice of a High Court.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is a member of which committee of the Parliament?
explanation: The CAG is the ex-officio member of the Public Accounts Committee, which scrutinises the reports of the CAG and the reports of the Finance Commission, besides examining the appropriation accounts.

q: The 100th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2018 relates to:
options: the creation of the National Judicial Appointments Commission
the reservation of one-third of seats for women
cooperative federalism and the right to earn in any part of India
the introduction of the Goods and Services Tax
explanation: The 100th Amendment introduced cooperative federalism through Article 280A and recognised the right to reside and earn in any part of India, which was inserted in Article 19(1)(g).

q: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 reduced the term of the Lok Sabha and the state legislative assemblies from:
explanation: The 42nd Amendment shortened the maximum term of the Lok Sabha and the state assemblies from five years to four years and extended the life of the incumbent governments; the 44th Amendment restored the five-year term.

q: The International Solar Alliance, co-founded by India and France, is headquartered at:
explanation: The International Solar Alliance, launched jointly by India and France in 2015, has its permanent secretariat at Gurugram in Haryana.

q: Under the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, the accounts of the municipalities are audited by:
options: the Comptroller and Auditor General of India or an auditor appointed by him
explanation: Article 149, inserted by the 74th Amendment, requires the accounts of the municipalities to be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General or by an auditor appointed by him.

q: In State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the Supreme Court held that:
options: the President alone may conduct foreign relations
treaties require the prior consent of every State
the Union Parliament may legislate on external affairs notwithstanding the State List
external affairs are a subject in the State List
explanation: The Court held that the Union Parliament has power to legislate on matters that are in the domain of external affairs, and that the power of the Parliament under Article 253 is not restricted by the State List.

q: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by:
options: the Chief Election Commissioner of India
the State Government in consultation with the Election Commission
explanation: Articles 243K and 243ZA provide that the State Election Commissioner shall be appointed by the Governor of the State, and his term and conditions are determined by the Governor.
